sections.h2: Law firms' generative AI use rose from 28% to 41% in a year

chart.title: Organisation-wide use of generative AI rose to 41% in one year
chart.sub: Share of law firms using generative AI across the organisation, %.
chart.source: Thomson Reuters, AI in Professional Services 2026 (a vendor survey).

sections.means: Adoption is climbing quickly, but the figures come from a survey run by a vendor that sells AI research tools to lawyers.
sections.todo: Firms should verify every AI-generated citation before relying on it, as the Supreme Court demanded of the Bar and the Bench.

sections.h2: Harvey's valuation rose from $5 billion to $15.5 billion since mid-2025

chart.title: Each Harvey funding round since June 2025 has raised its valuation
chart.sub: Harvey's valuation at each funding round, US$ billion.

sections.means: Investors have priced legal AI at billions of dollars in a few months, well ahead of any published evidence on how lawyers are paid.
sections.todo: Clients and firms should test whether AI tools change billable hours before assuming the billing model will shift.

sections.h2: India's fake-law entries mostly trace to the bench, not to lawyers

chart.title: Judges, tribunals and officers account for 11 of 16 Indian entries
chart.sub: Indian entries in the AI Hallucination Cases database, by who relied on the fake material.
chart.source: Damien Charlotin, AI Hallucination Cases database, India filter.

sections.means: In India the fake law reached decisions, not just court filings, which is why the Supreme Court addressed the Bench as well as the Bar.
sections.todo: The Bar Council of India should publish the AI rules the Supreme Court asked for, and this blog found none yet.

sections.h2: Legal research AI gave hallucinated answers in 17% to 33% of queries

chart.title: Even specialist legal research tools hallucinated in up to 33% of queries
chart.sub: Share of test queries with a hallucinated answer, %.
chart.source: Stanford RegLab, J. Empirical Legal Studies (2025).

sections.means: Specialist tools hallucinate less than a general chatbot, but not little enough to skip checking their output.
sections.todo: Lawyers should check every answer a research tool gives against the primary source before it reaches a court or a client.
